item.title: News Wrap: Defense rests in murder trial of Lindsay Clancy
item.description:
On Friday, the defense rested in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who has admitted to strangling her three young children to death. Closing arguments are expected early next week, after which the case will go to the jury. The 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse is on trial for three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her children at the family’s home in Duxbury, Massachusetts. Clancy’s children were 5 years old, 3 years old, and 8 months old. She has pleaded not guilty. The case has become a lightning rod with the public, largely because Clancy’s defense argues that she had postpartum psychosis at the time of the killings. Clancy’s defense team is relying on what’s commonly referred to as the insanity defense to argue that she was not criminally responsible because of her mental state. The state says Clancy was aware of what she was doing when she…

item.title: Lindsay Clancy suffering 'command hallucination' when she killed children, court hears
item.description:
Another summer, another high-profile trial for everyone to lose their mind over. There was Boston’s Karen Read in 2024, Amber Heard and Johnny Depp’s battle over who abused who worse a few years before that, and now, there’s the case of Lindsay Clancy. Clancy, whose legal team says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis , strangled her three children to death in the basement of her Massachusetts home in early 2023, and neither she nor her lawyers deny that. The murder trial that’s taking place now is to ascertain whether Clancy should spend the rest of her life in prison, or in a mental institution. But on some deep and feminine corners of the internet, there is a chorus growing who believe that Clancy is innocent, and allege that her husband, Patrick, is the one who committed the unspeakable crime. item.title: Search continues after deadly mine collapse on Cameroon-Central African Republic border
item.description:
The collapse was caused by a landslide, while local officials say the death toll is likely to rise as recovery efforts continue More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine at a small village in western Central African Republic (CAR) caved in due to a landslide, local officials and aid workers said on Wednesday. The landslide happened on Tuesday afternoon in the village of Zamboye, about 50km (31 miles) from the town of Baboua and close to the border of Cameroon. Footage on social media appeared to show an avalanche of sand descend on a group of people, likely the miners, and cover them. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry and Meghan moving back to Britain: reports
item.description:
Imagine, for a minute, that everyone in your neighborhood is paying your rent, and then, one day, you accuse them all of being racist bullies and move away. Imagine you accused your own family, too. You’re a grown man, and you tell your brother, who’s got three kids under the age of 10, that he wasn’t supportive enough. You complain because your father won’t let you use his credit card anymore. Back home, the neighborhood whispers that you left because your elderly grandmother’s late, beloved husband was a bigot—and you let everybody believe it. item.title: Prof. Musa Al-Gharbi's "Jason Arday and Me"
item.description:
A very interesting piece in the Chronicle of Higher Education . Here are two brief excerpts, but they can't do justice to the whole piece, which covers much more ground: {[W]hen a mainstream journalist [investigated Arday], he was threatened with lawsuits , visited by the police , and subsequently instructed by his editors to bury the story—and he sheepishly complied. Arday was exposed by a "race realist" Substack writer because reporters wouldn't cover the story until after it had already become common knowledge . It seems to defeat the purpose of the journalistic profession to tell people what they've already learned by other means, but that was the position U.K. media outlets and journalists took: radio silence until "others" started the conversation. And, somehow, the main lesson many seem to be taking from the way things played out is that we need even more media censorship…

item.title: Israel admits its soldiers fired at car in which Hind Rajab was killed
item.description:
A general view of the damaged car in which 5-year-old Hind Rajab and members of her family died after Israeli forces fired on the vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, Gaza. —Dawoud Abo Alkas—Anadolu/Getty Images The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has acknowledged for the first time that its soldiers opened fire on a vehicle carrying 5-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab and six of her relatives in Gaza, and said it would launch a criminal investigation into the incident. item.title: Palestinian teen shot and killed in West Bank attack, UN responds
item.description:
Report says violence is moving from Israeli-controlled areas to those earmarked for a future Palestinian state Violent Israeli settler attacks in the two areas of the occupied West Bank under direct Palestinian rule have almost doubled since 2025, as settlers pursue a self-proclaimed “great settlement revolution” in the very heart of the territory earmarked for a Palestinian state. According to a report by the Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din , shared with the Guardian, data shows that almost two-thirds of incidents of settler violence so far in 2026 have taken place in the so-called Areas A and B – placed under Palestinian Authority governance in the 1995 Oslo accords.
